Feedback

Purpose: tell users what happened. Persistent messages (alerts) and

Purpose: tell users what happened. Persistent messages (alerts) and transient notifications (toasts) are different components with different announcement contracts — read both before choosing.

Alerts (persistent, in-flow)

<div class="sq-alert sq-alert--success" role="status">
  <span class="sq-alert__icon" aria-hidden="true"><!-- svg --></span>
  <div class="sq-alert__body">
    <p class="sq-alert__title">Export ready</p>
    <p class="sq-alert__text">fleet-march.csv is in your downloads.</p>
  </div>
</div>

Tones: --success/--info/--warning/--error. Roles: role="status" (completion, polite) or role="alert" (errors that block, assertive). The tone border + icon + title triple Up the message — color is never alone. Alerts stay until resolved or dismissed by context (navigation, explicit close); they never auto-expire.

Toasts (transient, live region)

<div class="sq-toasts" data-sq-toasts role="status"></div>
<script>
  Squircle.notify("Workspace saved.", { tone: "success" });
  // { tone: "info"|"success"|"warning"|"error", duration: 6000(ms, 0=persist),
  //   region, dismissLabel } — dismissLabel (or the region's
  //   data-sq-toast-dismiss-label) localizes the dismiss button for SRs.
  const handle = Squircle.notify("Uploading…", { duration: 0 });
  handle.dismiss(); // or Squircle.dismissAll();
</script>

notify() takes plain text (never HTML — injection impossible by construction). Auto-dismiss pauses on hover/focus; an expiry that elapsed during the pause lands when the pause ends. Every toast has a dismiss button; errors assert (role="alert"), the rest are polite. Entrance is the gentle sq-rise-in rise — flattened to instant under reduced motion. Region-less calls before <body> exists are deferred to DOMContentLoaded instead of throwing.

The toast rule: if the user must act on it or find it later, it is not a toast — use an alert or inline text. Toasts supplement; they never carry the only copy of anything essential.

Progress, spinner, skeleton

<div class="sq-progress-label">
  <span>Uploading fleet.csv</span><span>62%</span>
</div>
<progress class="sq-progress" value="62" max="100">62%</progress>

<div role="status">
  <span class="sq-spinner" aria-hidden="true"></span>
  <span class="sq-spinner__label">Loading berth schedule…</span>
</div>

<div role="status" aria-label="Loading article…">
  <div class="sq-skeleton" style="height: 2rem; width: 60%"></div>
  <div class="sq-skeleton" style="height: 1rem"></div>
</div>
  • progress/meter are native: labeled outside, values announced

natively, sq-progress--large for hero moments.

  • Spinners pair the visual with a visually-hidden status label; under

reduced motion the ring freezes (still labeled, still honest).

  • Skeletons reserve the space they will fill (explicit heights/widths

— never auto-height shift); the shimmer becomes a static wash under reduced motion; the container names what loads.

Badges, status, empty states

<span class="sq-badge sq-badge--success">Live</span>
<span class="sq-status sq-status--warning"
  ><span class="sq-status__dot" aria-hidden="true"></span>Degraded</span
>

<div class="sq-empty">
  <span class="sq-empty__icon" aria-hidden="true"><!-- svg --></span>
  <p class="sq-empty__title">No exports yet</p>
  <p class="sq-empty__text">Exports you create appear here.</p>
  <a class="sq-button sq-button--primary" href="/export">Create an export</a>
</div>

Badge tones set fill + contrast ink; the LABEL carries meaning. Status dots are aria-hidden — the text announces. Empty states name what is missing, why, and the one next action (with a real link/button — never a dead end).

Banners (page-level, dismissible)

<div class="sq-banner sq-banner--info" id="maintenance-banner">
  <span class="sq-banner__icon" aria-hidden="true">
    <svg
      class="sq-icon"
      viewBox="0 0 24 24"
      fill="none"
      stroke="currentColor"
      stroke-width="2"
      stroke-linecap="round"
      stroke-linejoin="round"
      focusable="false"
    >
      <circle cx="12" cy="12" r="10" />
      <path d="M12 8h.01" />
      <path d="M11 12h1v4h1" />
    </svg>
  </span>
  <div class="sq-banner__body">
    <p class="sq-banner__title">Scheduled maintenance</p>
    <p class="sq-banner__text">
      The dispatch API pauses Sunday 02:00–04:00 CET.
    </p>
  </div>
  <button
    class="sq-banner__close"
    type="button"
    aria-label="Dismiss announcement"
    onclick="this.closest('.sq-banner').remove()"
  ></button>
</div>

Banner = alert styling at page level: --{success,info,warning,error} tones share the alert border system. Where it differs from an alert is intent: it sits ABOVE content, announces site-wide state (maintenance, bans, migrations), and dismisses with one button. Dismissal is HTML, not runtime state: the demo onclick removes the element; a real implementation moves it into your bundle (and may persist the choice in storage — an author decision, never Squircle's). Do not stack banners; the newest state replaces the older one.

Chips (tags with removal)

<div class="sq-chips">
  <span class="sq-chip"><span class="sq-chip__text">alloy</span></span>
  <span class="sq-chip sq-chip--success"
    ><span class="sq-chip__text">in stock</span></span
  >
  <span class="sq-chip">
    <span class="sq-chip__text">removable</span>
    <button
      class="sq-chip__remove"
      type="button"
      aria-label="Remove chip removable"
    ></button>
  </span>
</div>

Chips are badges with room for content and (optionally) a remove button. The remove button is a REAL button whose accessible name names the chip ("Remove chip alloy"); the glyph is drawn by CSS. The list wrapper keeps the group from floating loosely. Tone chips reuse the badge fill pairs. Chips are content tags — form-driven token entry (input + paste + Enter) is a pattern to compose with .sq-field, not a separate component (documented limitation).

Accessibility

  • Live regions: status (polite) vs alert (assertive) chosen by

urgency, not by habit. Dynamic content injected into a region on the page announces; regions created at notify-time announce on insertion.

  • Dismissal: toasts dismiss (button + timeout); alerts persist until

their context resolves.

  • Reduced motion: shimmer static, spinner frozen-but-labeled, toast

entrance instant. Nothing essential animates.

  • Contrast: all tones checked in both themes (fills + inks are

contrast-paired tokens).

Theme behavior

Tones, washes, inks, and shimmers are tokens. Error red is semantic-only (documented in tokens); everything else re-maps per theme without markup changes.

Customization

Override --sq-alert-*, --sq-badge-*, --sq-toast-*, --sq-skeleton-* or restyle tones later. Keep the border+icon+text triple — dropping to color-only breaks the contract.

Responsive behavior

Alerts grid (icon/text/action) wraps naturally; toasts center on narrow, dock right at 48rem+; empty states cap at measure. Toast max-width guards small viewports.

Common mistakes

  • Toast for errors the user must fix — alerts or inline errors.
  • role="alert" on every status — assertive interrupts; most news is polite.
  • Skeletons with no dimensions — layout shift is the bug skeletons exist to prevent.
  • Badge without text ("●" alone) — the dot is decoration; the label is the message.
  • Spinner without a status label — motion-only loading excludes everyone who cannot see it.
  • Banner for role-scoped state — banners are site-wide; use alerts in flow.
  • Chips whose remove button is an unlabeled glyph — name the chip.

Tested limitations

  • Toast stacking beyond ~4 is untested visually (regions scroll; keep counts low).
  • progress indeterminate state styling is platform-default (correct, unthemed).
  • No confirm-dialog patterns here — destructive confirmations live in OVERLAYS.md dialogs.
